title: Coulomb matrix not positive-definite (indefinite / non-Hermitian)
symptom: The reader-v1 full Coulomb family v1_coulomb_full_iq_*_rank*.dat is indefinite or non-Hermitian: the PSD/Hermitian gate reports a materially negative eigenvalue or a Hermitian residual above roundoff.
root_cause: The LU-based Coulomb-matrix inversion (exx_cs_inv_thr = -1) is numerically unstable for a large or near-singular auxiliary-basis set, especially for systems with localised d/f states or long-range screening. For strict-2D the legacy full-Ewald matrix can also be strongly indefinite because of large-number cancellation between the Ewald terms.
minimal_fix: Switch the inversion to matrix diagonalization by setting exx_cs_inv_thr to a positive value (1e-5 is the documented safe choice). For strict-2D, opt in to out_librpa_2d_coulomb_method direct_mixed_fourier. Never clip eigenvalues or substitute cut Coulomb to make a failed matrix pass.
validation: Re-run the stage.state/coulomb gate: the full matrix must be Hermitian to roundoff and have no materially negative eigenvalue relative to the largest eigenvalue and numerical norm.
avoid: Eigenvalue clipping, a smooth inverse, or substituting cut Coulomb for the production result. Do not relax the PSD gate to pass a failed matrix.
source: abacus-librpa-strict2d-direct-coulomb skill; ghj-stringent-dojo-exx-diagnostic; ~/.codex sessions on Coulomb-not-positive-definite.
